alerts.title: Overdue serum creatinine monitoring on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring every 12 months for patients on TDF. The patient's most recent creatinine was 88 umol/L on 2024-10-01, which is 478 days (over 15 months) before this visit. No creatinine was ordered at this encounter, creating a monitoring gap exceeding the 12-month interval. The clinician's plan notes routine follow-up with no issues and includes no renal function testing.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR now, as the patient is over 12 months since last renal function monitoring on TDF.

alerts.title: Viral load near suppression threshold
alerts.message: Guidelines define viral suppression as VL <200 copies/mL for plasma samples. The patient's viral load was 40 copies/mL on 2025-10-01, which is suppressed. However, per guidelines, adults require VL monitoring every 12 months after the initial 6- and 12-month tests if suppressed. The most recent VL was 113 days ago, so the next VL is not yet due. No action is needed at this visit.

evidence.recommended_action: No viral load action needed now; ensure next VL is scheduled at approximately 12 months from the 2025-10-01 test.

Given the above background and taking into consider the 2021 World Health Organization guidance to monitor low-level viremia, the guidelines have been designed to carter for health facilities with capacity to utilize plasma and dried blood spot (DBS) samples at suppression cut off points of 200 copies/ mL and 400 copies/mL respectively, as shown in Figure 58. A patient who has been on ART for more than 6 months and is responding to ART is considered virally suppressed at VL <200 copies/mL and <400 copies/mL for plasma and DBS samples, respectively. Facilities should constitute a multidisciplinary VL review committees to review, track, and make decisions to optimize ART regimen by switching to second-line, third- line, or a more potent regimen.
